answer.rationale:
The load-bearing memory for the tempting move is memory_c2 (switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor cut unit cost with quick onboarding). It is the only record that would justify a full primary switch 14 days before expiry, so it is the one worth spending the single verification pull on. What I need from the source record is the conditions it was earned under: what component class, what volume commitment, whether the line had slack at the time, and whether 'onboarding was quick' meant qualification/PPAP was already complete. The current situation has no buffer at 94% of committed volume, which is exactly the condition under which a fast switch stops being cheap.

Absent that verification, my intended action is to negotiate terms with the incumbent, using the low-cost vendor's quote as the benchmark. memory_c4 says benchmarking moved the incumbent on both price and payment terms; memory_c6 says term length unlocked volume pricing; memory_c1 says renewal avoided migration work and delivery interruption. Together those point at a path that can plausibly reach a large share of the 18% mandate without introducing qualification risk into a line with zero slack. I am keeping it small and guarded: a short-term or single-cycle instrument with an explicit option to add the low-cost vendor as a second source at next review (memory_c3), rather than a multi-year lock that would foreclose that.

Downstream risk I am flagging rather than absorbing: an 18% cut is a target that can be met on paper by trading away things that do not appear in unit price - expedite rights, allocation priority during shortage, inspection scope, payment flexibility. memory_c6's 'without narrowing the service scope' is precisely the clause that tends to quietly move when price is squeezed hard, so scope must be held explicitly in writing rather than assumed. I also note memory_c5 (defer preserved flexibility) does not transfer here: this contract does not auto-renew, so deferring is not a neutral hold, it is an unpriced gap against a line with no buffer.

Remaining uncertainty: I do not know whether negotiation alone closes the full 18%. If verification shows memory_c2 was earned on a comparable component with slack in the line and completed qualification, switching becomes materially more attractive and I would revise. If it was earned on a non-critical or already-qualified part, the memory does not license the switch here and negotiation is the right single decision this cycle.
